findings: Criterion 1 (oracle fitness and independence): The expected answers come from two retrieved public sources — the ChEMBL Interface Documentation ("-Log(molar IC50, XC50, EC50, AC50, Ki, Kd or Potency)" and "an IC50 measurement of 1nM would have a pChEMBL value of 9") and Papadatos et al. 2015 ("the negative logarithm of the activity values (in M units)"). Neither was written by the submitted skill or by the verifier, and Python has confirmed each key is quoted token-exactly from pinned bytes. The oracle's real weakness, which the design states openly, is that both sources are EMBL-EBI products describing the same database field and neither uses the literal token pIC50: they define pChEMBL, of which pIC50 is the IC50 instance. That identification is one unquoted inferential step, but it is an uncontroversial one for a definitional claim about a standard potency transform, and the documentation's own worked example is stated for an IC50 measurement specifically. Fit for purpose at B; the partial dependence of the two sources is exactly the kind of limited curation that bars A on the reference side independently of the case count.

Criterion 2 (coverage): Facts the statement and expected behaviour assert: (a) the transform is a base-10 logarithm — tested by pic50-one-nanomolar (natural log yields ~20.7, not 9) and by the natural-logarithm distractor in pic50-transform-shape; (b) the result is negated — tested by pic50-one-nanomolar (a positive 9 rather than -9) and by the un-negated 'logarithm' distractor in pic50-transform-shape; (c) the IC50 must be expressed in molar units before the transform — tested by pic50-required-units and, end to end, by pic50-one-nanomolar, where logging the bare nanomolar number gives 0; (d) the end-to-end conversion itself — tested by pic50-one-nanomolar. No fact the claim states is untested, so there is no coverage gap for which a listed reference bears or for which no search is recorded. Three trials per case is adequate for deterministic definitional answers. Coverage is thin in depth rather than in breadth: one worked magnitude only, and two of three cases are recognition — materially limited curation, which is what B describes.

Criterion 3 (comparison rule, tolerance, uncertainty): The numeric case is scored by the installed numeric comparison at 1e-6 absolute against the exact integer 9, so the tolerance absorbs only formatting (9 vs 9.0); the value is definitional and carries no measurement error, so no wider band is warranted and no narrower one is possible. The two choice cases are scored as an exact option index, which is the right rule for recognised answers. The stated uncertainty section is candid and accurate: single magnitude probed, two of three cases recognition, two partially dependent EMBL-EBI sources, pIC50-as-pChEMBL-instance asserted rather than quoted, and no spare case above the three-case minimum. Nothing is overstated.

Criterion 4 (stronger grade): A requires at least five counting cases with at least two generated; this design has three counting cases with one generated, so A is unreachable on both counts regardless of the reference side's quality. The justification's reason for not adding further open cases is weaker than it claims — the rubric's calculated-answers provision would have allowed further numeric conversions (e.g. other magnitudes, or the inverse direction) keyed by a program anchored on the quoted 1 nM to 9 worked example, so 'no quoted expected value' is not a sufficient reason. That is a missed opportunity to reach for A, not a defect that makes the present evidence weaker than B. As built, B is the strongest grade this evidence supports, and C would understate it since a genuine external oracle with quoted keys exists.
Criterion 5 (prior objections): prior_objections is empty, so there is nothing to resolve and nothing here counts for or against this version.

No case asks what a higher or lower pIC50 implies about potency, which the claim never states — correctly excluded.

pic50-one-nanomolar.reason: Open numeric case applying the full claim: 1 nM must be read as 1e-9 M and the negative base-10 logarithm taken. The key 9 is quoted verbatim from the ChEMBL FAQ's own worked example for an IC50 measurement. Both halves of the definition are discriminated — logging the bare nanomolar number gives 0, natural logs give ~20.7, omitting the negation gives -9. The stem states no part of the answer and the unit conversion it demands is within the claim, which requires molar expression.

pic50-required-units.reason: The claim's statement explicitly says IC50_in_M, so the required unit is part of what it asserts, not a consequence beyond it. The key word 'molar' is absent from the stem; the three prefixed molar units and the mass-per-volume option are all live wrong answers for a reader who logs whatever number the table holds. Answering from the claim alone gives option 3 unambiguously, so 'none of these' is not defensible. Overlaps with the open case's unit step, which bears on strength only.

pic50-transform-shape.reason: Isolates the functional form the claim asserts: distractors drop the negation, change the base, and substitute reciprocal and square root. No option mentions units, so the case cannot be answered from the unit fact tested by the sibling case, and all six options share the same 'the X of the activity values' shape, so the key is not marked by wording or style. From the claim alone, option 2 is the only defensible choice; the key's omission of the base is harmless since option 5 covers plain log and option 3 natural log.
